Purpose These accessory dwelling unit ("ADU") standards are intended to permit the creation of legal ADUs that are compatible with residential neighborhoods while also adding housing options for the Town’s workforce, seniors, families with changing needs, and others.
Generally

items.label: a
items.text: ADUs shall only be permitted on lots or parcels where the principal use is a single-family detached dwelling. An ADU is not allowed on a site without a principal dwelling unit.

items.label: b
items.text: Not more than one ADU may be located on one lot or parcel.

items.label: c
items.text: ADUs shall not have more than one bedroom.

items.label: d
items.text: Parking for the ADU shall be provided on the principal lot or parcel.

items.label: e
items.text: ADUs shall not exceed 40 percent of the square footage of the principal dwelling unit.

items.label: f
items.text: ADUs shall have a separate exterior entrance from the principal dwelling unit and shall contain separate cooking, sleeping, and sanitary facilities.
Standards for Detached ADUs

items.label: a
items.text: Detached ADUs shall meet the setback requirements of the principal building.

items.label: b
items.text: The building design standards applicable to the principal structure on the lot shall apply.

items.label: c
items.text: The maximum height of any detached ADU shall be 25 feet.

items.label: d
items.text: Detached ADUs shall comply with the requirements for accessory structures in §4.4. Where one or more of the standards in §4.4 conflict with these use-specific standards, these use-specific standards shall govern.
Owner Occupancy

items.label: a
items.text: Ownership of the ADU may not be legally severed from ownership of the associated lot and any other structures on such lot.

items.label: b
items.text: The owner of each property on which an ADU is located shall sign an affidavit pledging agreement with the terms of this section. The affidavit shall specify which dwelling unit (either the primary dwelling unit or the ADU) the owner will occupy. If at any time the owner moves from one dwelling unit to the other, the owner shall file an updated affidavit. Otherwise, all affidavits shall be filed annually with the Development and Neighborhood Services Department.
Noticing

items.label: a
items.text: The Town shall notice to all persons owning land within 200 linear feet from the subject parcel(s) for which an ADU is being requested.

items.label: b
items.text: Mailed notices shall be postmarked and sent via first class mail after the application is deemed complete and prior to final approval.

items.label: c
items.text: The mailed notice shall include:

items.label: i
items.text: The physical address, zoning designation, and principal use of the subject property;

items.label: ii
items.text: A brief narrative summarizing the request and demonstrating compliance with this section;

items.label: iii
items.text: The location and hours where a copy of the application can be examined by the public; and

items.label: iv
items.text: Any other information pertinent to the petition as deemed appropriate by the Director.
Operator Residency Required The operator of the home occupation shall reside in the dwelling unit.
Maximum Number of Nonresident Employees Any home occupation shall be permitted a maximum of one employee who does not reside in the dwelling unit.
Maximum Gross Floor Area

items.label: a
items.text: No more than 15 percent of the total gross floor area of the dwelling unit may be used in connection with the home occupation. However, no home occupation shall be limited to less than 200 square feet, nor shall the area of a home occupation exceed 500 square feet.

items.label: b
items.text: If there is more than one home occupation being conducted within a dwelling unit, then all home occupations within the dwelling unit shall cumulatively use no more than 15 percent or 500 square feet of the dwelling unit, whichever is less.

items.label: c
items.text: Area used for storage of materials or products used in the home occupation shall be included in this calculation.
Multiple Home Occupations

items.label: a
items.text: More than one home occupation may be permitted within an individual dwelling unit.

items.label: b
items.text: Where multiple home occupations are conducted within an individual dwelling unit, the operations standards of this section shall be applied to the combined total of all home occupation activities, not to each home occupation individually.

Residential Character There shall not be any interior or exterior, structural or aesthetic, alterations that change the residential character of the dwelling unit within which the home occupation operates.
Location and Entrance

items.label: a
items.text: The home occupation shall be conducted entirely within the principal structure or attached garage.

items.label: b
items.text: The use of an attached garage for a home occupation shall not interfere with the provision of any required off-street parking.
Outdoor Display and Storage Outdoor display of goods, materials, supplies, or equipment is prohibited.
Off-Street Parking and Loading No additional driveway to serve the home occupation shall be permitted.
Commercially Licensed Vehicles No vehicles requiring the operator to have a commercial driver's license shall be allowed in conjunction with any home occupation.
Deliveries Deliveries to the property shall not be permitted, except those by typical residential delivery services at a similar frequency as homes that do not operate a home occupation.
Kitchen facilities may be permitted only as accessory uses within a Residence Hotel.
Kitchenette facilities may be permitted only as accessory uses within a Hotel, Full Service or Hotel, Limited Service.

Any valet parking service provided in connection with a commercial establishment or commercial activity shall obtain a license and comply with the standards established in the Administrative Manual. A license shall not be required for occasional valet parking service provided:
At a private residence; or
In connection with a social or fund-raising activity.

Contractor's offices, equipment storage, and portable lavatories are permitted on or adjacent to construction sites on lots or parcels owned or controlled by the owner of the lot or parcel on which the construction is taking place, subject to following:

Construction support activities may only be approved for licensed contractors working on construction projects for which permits have been issued. They shall be located on the same lot or parcel and within the same project area where the work is being performed and shall not encroach into any public right-of-way. Field or construction or offices shall be required to meet all applicable state and local building and set-up codes.
The use shall only occur between 14 days before and 14 days after the construction activity. All temporary facilities shall be removed within 14 days after completion of construction.
The Building Official may order the construction support activities to be discontinued.
The structures shall not contain sleeping or cooking facilities.
Portable lavatories shall be located on-site as to minimize impacts to adjacent uses.
Location

items.label: a
items.text: Food trucks and associated seating areas shall not be located in any required landscaping area, access easement, driveway, or fire lane(s).

items.label: b
items.text: All eating, drinking, service, and delivery activity shall occur outside of setbacks, landscaping, and the public right-of-way.
Site Design

items.label: a
items.text: Mobile food vending equipment shall be placed on improved surfaces.

items.label: b
items.text: The site shall provide at least 250 square feet in space for each individual food truck. There shall be at least three feet of clearance between each individual food truck and between each permanent or accessory structure and at least 10 feet of unobstructed clearance for food trucks parked side-by-side.

items.label: c
items.text: There is no limit to the total number of food trucks allowed on a site provided adequate fire access is maintained on site.

items.label: d
items.text: Each mobile food truck shall provide trash receptables sized to meet expected demand and shall empty or remove them on a daily basis.
Operational Standards

items.label: a
items.text: A Temporary Use Permit for a mobile food truck shall not exceed 90 days.

items.label: b
items.text: A food service license is required and shall be available on site for inspection by government officials.

items.label: c
items.text: Each individual food truck shall contain an electrical hookup or generator, meet Fire Code, and maintain access to a commercial kitchen within Dallas County.

items.label: d
items.text: When located adjacent to a Residential zoning district, the hours of operation shall be limited between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.

items.label: e
items.text: All mobile food trucks shall return to their associated restaurant, a commissary kitchen, or other base of operation for necessary vehicle servicing, cleaning, and restocking on a daily basis. Overnight parking is prohibited.
Operational Standards

items.label: a
items.text: A Temporary Use Permit shall only be issued to the operator of the associated permanent retail use.

items.label: b
items.text: The outdoor retail and display uses shall be associated with an approved retail primary use on the property.

items.label: c
items.text: The outdoor retail and display area shall be of the same nature as the permanent retail activity conducted on the property.

items.label: d
items.text: The outdoor retail and display areas shall be kept clean and free from litter, refuse, and debris;

items.label: e
items.text: Outdoor retail and display operations shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including but not limited to those regulating the sale of alcohol, preparation and sale of food, and noise ordinances.

items.label: f
items.text: The outdoor retail and display areas shall comply with all other reasonable conditions imposed by the Development and Neighborhood Services Department.
Location and Design

items.label: a
items.text: The outdoor retail and display area shall be contained on an improved surface such as asphalt, concrete, or pavers, and such areas shall be limited to 15 percent of the gross floor area of the principle structure.

items.label: b
items.text: The outdoor retail and display area shall not block handicapped parking areas, parking lot access aisles, sidewalk areas, fire lanes, required landscape areas, public rights-of-way, pedestrian ways, and shall not reduce the number of parking spaces below any minimum requirement for the use in this UDC.
Duration and Frequency In those zoning districts where §4.2.7: Table of Allowed Uses, indicates that outdoor retail and display is a temporary use:

items.label: a
items.text: Outdoor retail and display areas shall be allowed for a period not to exceed 14 days each calendar year, with a maximum of two permits issued per business, per calendar year.

items.label: b
items.text: The 14-day time period is limited to the actual days and times of the event, except that set-up activities may occur up to 48 hours prior to the permitted event and take-down/clean-up activities may occur up to 24 hours after the permitted event.
No more than one portable storage structure may be located on the same lot or parcel at one time.
Portable storage structures shall be located no closer than 10 feet to any property line and shall be placed on an improved surface.
A portable storage structure may be located on a lot or parcel for a period not exceeding 14 consecutive days, from the time of delivery to the time of removal.

Portable storage structures shall not be located on the same lot or parcel more than one time in any given 30-calendar-day period. Each day that a portable storage structure remains after the removal date shall constitute a violation.
Portable storage structures shall not exceed eight feet six inches in height, 10 feet in width, nor 20 feet in length.

It shall be the obligation of the owner or user of the portable storage structure to secure it in a manner that does not endanger the safety of persons or property in the vicinity of the portable storage structure. In the event of high winds or other weather conditions in which such structure may become a physical danger to persons or property, the appropriate law enforcement officers may require the immediate removal of the portable storage structure.
Any portable storage structure shall be removed immediately upon the direction of a law enforcement officer for removal of such temporary structure for safety reasons

4.5.5.E.title: Real Estate Sales or Model Home

items.text: Real estate sales or model homes are permitted on the site of the development for which the sales are taking place. They are permitted to remain on the site of the development from 15 days before homes are offered for sale until 15 days after all home or home sites within the development are sold.
The Building Official may order the removal or discontinuance of real estate sales or model home uses.
Generally

items.label: a
items.text: Except for seasonal sales allowed pursuant to F.2 below, seasonal sales shall be located on a lot or parcel that fronts a collector or arterial street.

items.label: b
items.text: Seasonal sales areas shall not block handicapped parking areas, parking lot access aisles, sidewalk areas, fire lanes, required landscape areas, public rights-of-way, pedestrian ways, and shall not reduce the number of parking spaces below any minimum requirement for the use in this UDC;

items.label: c
items.text: Temporary tents, structures, or stands used for seasonal sales shall not exceed 150 square feet.

items.label: d
items.text: Temporary Use Permits issued for seasonal sales shall be valid for a maximum of 30 consecutive days.

items.label: e
items.text: No lot or parcel shall be issued more than three seasonal sales Temporary Use Permits in a calendar year.

R-1, R-2, and R-3 Zoning Districts Seasonal sales shall be limited to those activities that would not qualify as a special event, including the sale of fruits, vegetables, flowers, herbs, plants, jams, honey, pickled products, sauces, and/or baked goods where the vendors are individuals who have raised the produce or have crafted the product on the same lot or parcel where the seasonal sales are taking place.

Temporary use permits for other special events not listed separately in §4.2.7: Table of Allowed Uses, including but not limited to temporary wholesale activities, festivals, concerts, carnivals, and traveling circuses, shall be valid for a maximum of 14 consecutive days.

No property shall be issued more than six Temporary Use Permit in a calendar year. Organized community events sponsored by the Town and located on publicly owned land are exempt from this requirement.
